articles.title: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72
articles.summary: Efforts to recover bodies after a “double-tap” attack in southern Ukraine are being hampered by continuing Russian strikes, officials say.
articles.body: Ukrainian officials have accused Russia of targeting rescue and recovery operations two weeks after a deadly "double-tap" strike at a village close to the front line killed at least 72 people. Ukraine says Russia carried out two attacks in succession on a humanitarian aid centre in the village of Komyshuvakha on 2 November - including the use of what it said was a 3,000kg (6,600lb) aerial bomb on a shelter where residents had fled for safety. Verified images posted in the days after the attack show damage to emergency vehicles and excavation equipment at the site. The State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS) told BBC Verify there were multiple Russian strikes during the rescue. The DSNS said three police officers, four workers and two rescue dogs were injured while five vehicles were damaged during the operation, which has now concluded. With the DSNS saying the death toll had risen to at least 72 people, the attack on Komyshuvakha has become the second deadliest single incident of the Ukraine war. Oleksiy, an intelligence officer investigating the incident for Ukraine's SBU security service, who asked to be identified only by his first name, said rescue vehicles were "clearly marked" and accused Russia of "deliberately destroying humanitarian equipment". He added the village's infrastructure and the people still living in Komyshuvakha are also being systematically targeted by drones and bombs. Oleksiy accused Russian forces of "outright terror against civilians, against peaceful residents" to make life on the front line impossible. BBC Verify has confirmed videos being shared by Ukrainian police that show rescue workers at the scene shouting "drone, drone" and running for cover on the day after the 2 November attack. A group can also be seen treating a victim. Oleksiy said rescue crews operated under a constant threat of attack. "The enemy knows perfectly well that what is being carried out there is essentially a humanitarian operation to search for the dead," he said. BBC Verify has asked the Russian Ministry of Defence for comment specifically about the Komyshuvakha attacks but has not received a response. A general statement released on 2 November by the Russian MoD said it had targeted energy and transport infrastructure used by the Ukrainian military across the country. While there are no military or industrial facilities in Komyshuvakha it is close to a key route used for Ukrainian troop movements, supplies and evacuations. The village was previously reported to have been struck by the Russians on 28 October. Local people headed to the shelter area on 2 November after being told by a local Telegram group that aid would be distributed between 10:00 and 12:00 local time (08:00-10:00 GMT). Ukrainian authorities said an initial strike, at 09:45 local time, hit buildings above ground killing one woman. Video shows moments between deadly Russian attacks on village in Ukraine Bodycam footage, released by Ukrainian police in edited segments and analysed by BBC Verify, shows people trying to free a casualty from the rubble before declaring she had died. Throughout the footage, warnings of an impending second strike can be heard on police radios with increasing urgency until people are instructed to run to the underground shelter. The same footage, which was taken around an hour after the first attack, goes on to show people in a shelter. As they wait in silence a large explosion can be heard and the video goes dark. Aftermath video filmed later shows bodies being recovered from a large crater immediately above the shelter. Twisted iron and rubble from the structure below can be seen beneath the surface. Funerals have been held almost daily for the victims of the attack, including locals working to administer aid distribution, those seeking to collect it and soldiers who officials say arrived to assist with rescue efforts. Trevor Ball, bomb disposal expert at intelligence firm at Armament Research Services, said a crater seen in the footage was consistent with the damage and depth left by a FAB-3000, a 3,000kg Russian bomb which can destroy underground structures. His comments were echoed by Chris Proops, an ex-UK National Crime Agency investigator, who said the scale of the damage at the scene matched the size of the FAB-3000. Ball and Proops both confirmed verified photos of munition fragments obtained by BBC Verify from Ukrainian authorities show part of a guidance kit that is compatible with the FAB-3000, which increases the weapon's accuracy and allows it to be fired from a greater distance from the target. International law experts told BBC Verify that Russia had committed a war crime if it knowingly attacked rescue workers. Ben Saul, professor of international law at the University of Sydney, said this "appears to be either a deliberate attack on civilians or civilian objects - a war crime - or an indiscriminate attack - also a war crime". Prof Samuel Moyn of Yale University said "directly targeting rescuers or their equipment is a gross violation of international humanitarian law". Precautions have to be taken to ensure that strikes target combatants rather than others, he added.

articles.title: EU’s Kallas fights to find a role in Ukraine peace talks
articles.summary: Bloc's top diplomat said foreign ministers want a more direct role in Ukraine peace talks after leaders selected a team of national security advisers for the job.
articles.body: Bloc’s top diplomat said foreign ministers want a more direct role in Ukraine peace talks after leaders selected a team of national security advisers for the job. BRUSSELS — Kaja Kallas is scrambling to establish a role for herself in Ukraine peace talks after being excluded from the team negotiating on Europe’s behalf. The EU’s chief diplomat has repeatedly said she is the bloc’s top foreign policy official under EU treaties, while leading behind-the-scenes efforts to define the negotiators’ mandate — shaping what Europe should push for and where its red lines lie. “Take out the treaties and read the treaties,” she told reporters in Brussels when asked about her absence from the team negotiating the biggest security crisis Europe has faced in decades. “Who is dealing with the security and foreign policy issues? So, as we always say to our partners, rule of law actually in Europe is the treaties … So I stand by my words. And I’m ready to do this job [negotiating] as well.” After weeks of agonized debates over who should lead U.S.-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine, European Council President António Costa announced in Dublin last week that the team would include national security advisers from France, Germany, Poland, Italy and the U.K., plus representatives from the European Commission and Council. Kallas was not among them. The foreign ministers of Spain and Lithuania both criticized this approach as they arrived at a gathering in Brussels on Monday. “Europe needs one voice. We cannot speak with 27 microphones,” said Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys. “We need one and for that we need a clear mandate, clear procedures, [for] how we are agreeing on our joint position.” Some EU diplomats point to Kallas’s criticism of U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration as part of the reason she isn’t on the negotiation team. Others say the team is deliberately made up of national security officials who report directly to leaders, noting that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has not been involved in recent rounds of talks. While one national official involved in talks with Russia said Kallas was too divisive to be included, two EU diplomats argued the choice reflected a broader downgrading of foreign policy officials in global affairs. They were granted anonymity to speak frankly about the negotiating strategy, like others in the story. “This is part of a mega-trend that’s hard to fight,” said one of the diplomats. “More and more international questions that were once handled by foreign ministers are now being handled by prime ministers or presidents.” The key for Kallas and EU foreign ministers is to seek relevance by providing “geopolitical strategic perspective” on issues, even if they aren’t being directly consulted, the diplomat said. Envoys from the bloc’s 27 capitals had expressed a desire to play a more direct role in the Ukraine negotiations, Kallas said after her meeting of foreign affairs ministers in Brussels on Monday. “What many member states, ministers said, is that they don’t want to be debriefed about these things. They want to be, you know, involved in these talks.” “We have already prepared, with the foreign ministers, maximum demands,” she added, referring to a document laying out concessions for Russia to grant before talks could continue. Foreign ministers will work in coming weeks to refine these demands, drafting a negotiating mandate for Europe’s negotiating team in time for the next round of talks in Abu Dhabi, an EU official said. Yet other officials have said this job is likely to fall to EU ambassadors rather than foreign ministers, feeding into reports of a turf war between EU institutions over who controls foreign policy. In addition to leading the way on Ukraine, President Ursula von der Leyen’s Commission has also largely taken over managing relations between the EU and Israel, duplicating a department that previously handled relations with the Middle East and North Africa and sat within Kallas’ European External Action Service. Adding to the unease is a Franco-German effort to overhaul the EEAS by potentially integrating it more fully with the Commission in what some officials see as an attempt to bring the top diplomat job under control of the EU executive. For those involved in the talks, the explanation is simpler: They are happening at the level of national security advisers, not foreign policy heavyweights like Kallas. They point to Rubio’s absence from recent rounds, as well as that of Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov. While U.S. envoys said last week that Russia was open to letting Europeans join the peace negotiations, the Kremlin said Monday that no such agreement had been reached.

articles.title: Serbia's Parliament To Meet For First Time Since Opposition's Landslide Election Victory
articles.summary: Three weeks after winning a landslide election victory, Serbia's Student List opposition movement gets to flex its new political muscles as the country's parliament meets for the first time on November 17.
articles.body: BELGRADE -- Three weeks after winning a landslide election victory , Serbia's Student List opposition movement gets to flex its new political muscles as the country's parliament meets for the first time on November 17. The initial focus is electing a new speaker but the gathering of lawmakers also sets the clock ticking on electing a new government, a process that must be completed within 90 days. The Student List has 140 seats in the 250-seat parliament, putting it in the driver's seat after 14 years dominated by former President Aleksandar Vucic . But the leaderless movement has yet to say who it will nominate for speaker, prime minister, or other top jobs. Who's In Charge? The Faces Of Serbia's Student-Backed Political Movement Milan Bogunovic, a former veterinary surgeon who was elected for the Student List, told RFE/RL's Balkan Service that the main task at hand was rolling back the authoritarian system established by the Vucic years. "Establishing the rule of law, ensuring respect for the law, and making the system function properly. Everything that has failed to work over the years must start working," he said. His words were echoed by his colleague Mirza Ramusovic, a 35-year-old lawyer from Novi Pazar in southwest Serbia, where the majority of the population is Bosniak. "After 14 years of political stagnation and hopelessness, we have a new opportunity to implement reforms and chart a new course for Serbia," he told RFE/RL. The Student List emerged from a student movement that spent two years leading mass anti-government protests and insisted on accountability for the collapse of the canopy at Novi Sad railway station on November 1, 2024, which killed 16 people. Arrests, Resignations, Repainting: Here's What's Happening In Postelection Serbia Its platform is centered on fighting corruption and organized crime, ensuring the independence of the judiciary and prosecution service, and safeguarding media freedom. It's an important role, whose holder plays a large part in setting the legislative agenda. In addition to this, the new speaker will also be acting president following Vucic's resignation in June. A new presidential election must be held by the end of the year. Until the election of a new speaker, the parliament is chaired by its oldest serving member -- in this case, 78-year-old mathematician Stojan Radenovic, elected on Vucic's United Serbia list. Vucic will lead the United Serbia faction in parliament, of which his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) is the key member. The party did not respond to RFE/RL questions for this article, but Vucic has pledged it "will behave decently and responsibly" in opposition. Political scientist Dusko Radosavljevic said the SNS had never learned how to behave in a parliamentary manner. The previous majority was frequently accused of failing to respect parliamentary procedures. Over the years, neither bills nor amendments proposed by the opposition were accepted. While presiding over parliamentary sessions, former Speaker Ana Brnabic was often criticized for bias, selective application of the rules of procedure, and restricting opposition lawmakers from speaking. Nebojsa Vladisavljevic, a professor at the Faculty of Political Sciences in Belgrade, told RFE/RL that the character of the new parliament would be shaped by its expert composition. "The Student List is an expert-driven list, a kind of technocratic ticket, with a large number of PhDs and university professors," he said. "Citizens were clearly dissatisfied with the way experienced opposition politicians had operated." Radosavljevic said the backgrounds of the Student List legislators could also led to better laws. "When substantive legislation is debated, whether it concerns education, health care, or agriculture, there will be many people who genuinely understand those issues," he said.

articles.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
articles.summary: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.
articles.body: Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals. Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements. The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin. Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said. The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024 . Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest". Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said the plan to open a centre in Rwanda had no "future or humanity", according to AFP news agency. "I don't see any future or humanity in that. It's not the solution," Sanchez told the Spanish broadcaster Telecinco, AFP reported. The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights. The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc. In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean. In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda". Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system. Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants". He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration". Ahead of the announcement, diplomatic sources told the AFP news agency the hub is expected to initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending about 20 migrants. The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role. "IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms". With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration. Concerns around security, struggling economies and disillusionment with governing parties have all had a major role in shaping attitudes towards people leaving their home countries . Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would be a cause of concern as it had a "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo. "Paying Kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad." The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights argued any third country hosting a return hub should "respect fundamental rights", including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution. The agency added that unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, which the Dutch government has confirmed will not take place. According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026, which represents a 29% decrease compared to the previous year. In October, about 18,100 crossings were detected, which is about 6% less than October 2025 but 22% more than in September "largely because of a sharp rise in arrivals on the Western African route to the Canary Islands". articles.title: Houthis accuse Saudi Arabia of strikes that killed 3 including a child, and other Mideast news
articles.summary: The Iran-backed Houthi rebels blamed Saudi Arabia on Monday for two strikes that killed three people in Houthi-controlled Yemen. The Saudi government did not immediately comment.
articles.body: The Iran-backed Houthi rebels blamed Saudi Arabia on Monday for two strikes that killed three people in Houthi-controlled Yemen. The Saudi government did not immediately comment. Iran said Monday that three oil tankers caught fire when they struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. And Israel's military said it struck an arms shipment from Syria intended to reach Hezbollah in Lebanon. Here is the latest news from the Middle East on Monday. Read our full coverage here. Houthi health authorities said Monday that three Yemenis, including a child, were killed in two separate strikes in areas controlled by the Iran-backed rebels. The child was killed in a drone strike on a house in the al-Sarar quarter of the capital, Sanaa, that also wounded seven others, Health Ministry spokesperson Anees al-Asbahi said. WATCH: News Wrap: Britain sending air support to Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks Separate airstrikes Monday morning hit a private fuel station, killing two people and wounding eight in Harf Sufian district in Omran province, 50 kilometers (31 miles) north of Sanaa, al-Asbahi said. Al-Asbahi blamed Saudi Arabia, which made no immediate comment. The Houthis and the Saudis began fighting again in July, shattering a 2022 ceasefire that had largely stopped clashes in Yemen's civil war. Iran's state TV said three oil tankers caught fire overnight and early morning Monday after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Quoting the naval arm of the Revolutionary Guard and the army, the report warned shipping companies that a U.S.-supported route remains dangerous because of mines. The report offered no details on possible casualties or which flags the tankers were sailing under. Mines have damaged six oil tankers since Sunday and pollution has affected the strait's coastlines, according to the Revolutionary Guard's navy. Separately, a projectile struck a tanker attempting to transit through the strait, starting a fire in the engine room, but no casualties were reported, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Organization said. The waterway through which a fifth of the world's oil and gas supply transits in peacetime has become the focal point of the U.S.-Iran conflict. The Israeli military said it struck a shipment of weapons intended for Hezbollah on Monday near the village of Janta in northeastern Lebanon close to the border with Syria. It was the first time in months the Israeli military said it struck an area deep inside Lebanon. Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported no casualties from the airstrike in the eastern Baalbek region. The latest Israel-Hezbollah war ended with a U.S.-brokered ceasefire on June 20. But the Israeli military, which occupies dozens of towns and villages in southern Lebanon, has carried out detonations and airstrikes in the areas close to Israel's borders. The European Union announced new sanctions on a Gaza social media outlet and its founder on Monday over alleged fundraising for militant groups. For soliciting funds for Hamas, both Gaza Now and its 34-year-old founder Mustafa Ayash will have their EU assets frozen. Ayash, who has refugee status in Austria, will be banned from travel within the 27-nation EU. The outlet has over 470,000 followers on X and was sanctioned by the United States in 2024. Israeli police announced an internal probe Monday into their handling of allegations of voter fraud during last month's elections. The announcement follows reports that a top aide to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu tipped off police about possible voter bribing in the Arab sector, leading to the arrests of seven men on suspicion of buying votes for an Arab-led party. All were released for lack of evidence. LISTEN: What Israel's election deadlock means for Netanyahu and the region The police commissioner said the investigation will look into allegations in the Israeli media that police improperly made the arrests based on faulty intelligence. Netanyahu has repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims that the election was "stolen" by Arab voters after his parliamentary bloc lost its majority. Israel's election commission found " no evidence of irregularities " affecting the results, but the domestic intelligence agency Shin Bet is still investigating claims of foreign interference. United Nations ambassador Mike Waltz told reporters in Beirut after talks with Lebanese leaders on Monday that the U.S. and France are working to reach a consensus in the U.N. Security Council about the future of the U.N. peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon. Walz said the force will will continue with some modifications after its current mandate ends at the end of the year. WATCH: On the ground with UN peacekeepers as Lebanon-Israel mission nears its end Waltz, who met with Lebanon's president, parliament speaker and prime minister, said Lebanese sovereignty must be fully restored. He said the militant Hezbollah group must disarm, saying no country should have "two armies." The European Saudi Organization for Human Rights identified the two men on Monday as Jawad Abdullah Qureiris and Fadel Hassan al-Safwani. They were executed Saturday in the Eastern Province. Al-Safwani, the activist, helped organize protests in the eastern city of Qatif calling for civil rights and the release of detainees. Qureiris was 16 when he took part in the protests. Both were detained in 2020 and were among 210 people executed in Saudi Arabia so far this year, according to the rights group. Bahrain on Monday sentenced dozens of Shiite clerics to life in prison over terrorism-related charges. Rights groups said the mass trial was marred by allegations of torture and violations of due process. The Bahrain High Criminal Court sentenced 64 defendants to life imprisonment and five others each received 15 years in prison, according to the Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy. The defendants were convicted of various charges including establishing a terrorist group with the aim of overthrowing the government. They also were convicted of promoting Iran's style of governance, known as "the Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist." One defendant was accused of espionage for Iran, the rights group said.

US and Iran slide closer to fresh all-out war as new exchange of fire increases
articles.summary: A sudden rise in Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz follows an increasing number of air strikes between the US and Iran, as both sides trade intensifying warning shots, bringing the region closer to a new all-out war. Meanwhile, a third US aircraft carrier has arrived in the region.
articles.body: The US and Iran have conducted widening airstrikes in a fast-moving cycle of violence since Sunday, while Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said two more oil tankers exploded in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, bringing the total number of tankers that caught fire in the waterway to six, since Sunday.The US military launched new airstrikes on Iranian missile launchers across southern Iran on Sunday night after Iranian forces attacked a US base in Bahrain and fired missiles at tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Amid this significant escalation across the region, the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier has now arrived to join two other carrier strike groups in US CENTCOM's operating region.Iran targeted Bahrain twice over the last weekend, for the first time in months since the Iran war subsided, conducting a drone attack on the US helicopter compound at Al Riffa Air Base on Sunday, in response to previous US strikes. US CENTCOM denied any damage to US assets, as Iran appears to be ramping up its warnings and show force using attacks on Gulf states again.Iran also attacked tankers in Hormuz which usually triggers immediate US strikes on Iran’s coastal military infrastructure.The US military then struck Iranian launchers in Bandar Lengeh and Sirik in southern Iran on Sunday night, targetting a wider area than the previous strike cycles and with a higher rate of fire by both sides.Flight tracking portals registered a much larger US Air Force presence over the Persian Gulf in the region than in the previous weeks, just as the US is continuing its military build-up.More tankers struck in the Strait of HormuzThe IRGC said on Sunday that two tankers were trying to cross the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz under direct US military guidance when they allegedly encountered naval mines that "lit up the skies for hours", Iran's Tasnim news agency reported.The IRGC described the actions as a response to what it called the "illegal US blockade" and violation of Iranian regulations in the Strait of Hormuz, warning oil companies again that the southern route of the waterway was mined.Then on Monday, Iran’s Navy announced that a "violator" oil tanker caught fire after colliding with a sea mine in the restricted area east of the Strait of Hormuz and was unable to move.“Turning off tracking systems and unauthorised entry into prohibited and unsafe maritime areas exposes offending vessels to serious risks,” Iran’s Navy said in a statement.It was not clear whether the tanker is one of six tankers reported by the IRGC to have caught fire, or if a separate incident occurred, and claims by the IRGC and the army about the number of tankers damaged and details of the explosions have not been independently confirmed.However, the UK's Maritime Trade Operations Authority (UKMTO) issued a statement confirming that it had received reports of at least one incident in the early hours of Monday morning when an oil tanker was hit by "an unidentified projectile" while passing out of the Strait of Hormuz."The collision led to a fire in the engine room," the report said, adding that so far no casualties have been reported and all crew members are safe and that "the assessment of the damage and the extent of the environmental damage is currently unclear."Oil prices rose on Monday following the large number of vessels incidents in the Strait of Hormuz.Third US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle EastThe USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier arrived in the CENTCOM area of operations in the region, joining the USS George Washington and USS George H.W. Bush carrier strike groups, marking the first time since the Iraq war that the US has three carriers in the Middle East.The US military is now completing a massive build-up of naval and air strike capabilities of approximately 19 US warships in the region, including the Red Sea, with guided missile destroyers and cruisers alongside other naval forces.Meanwhile, the Wall Street Journal quoted US intelligence analysts who assess in a low confidence estimate that Iran now has between 1,500 and 2,500 new missiles in addition to new drones and short-range missiles, while Israeli military officials place Iran’s new capabilities at 1,500 ballistic missiles.On 10 November, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) released a picture claiming to show the head of Iran’s armed forces and the IRGC Aerospace Force commander touring tunnels with missiles and launchers which they called a new underground “missile city.”The Iranian regime has continued its threats against renewed US wide-scale attacks, with military officials telling Iranian Tabnak News on Sunday that "Iran's new offensive military doctrine means that the country will no longer be limited to calculated retaliation and will break the cycle of escalation," and threatening US bases in Europe too.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio lashed out at the “Shia clerics of Iran” on Sunday, stating that “every problem in the Middle East, every major problem in the Middle East – the Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia, the Shia militias that destabilize Iraq, the fighting elements that supported Assad and the destruction of Syria, Hizballah in Lebanon – everywhere you turn, there is one common denominator: the Shia clerics of Iran and their expansionist mentality.”“This is an extraordinary historic danger and one that cannot be ignored,” Rubio warned.As both sides appear to intensify their warning shots to build pressure and force concessions, the former head of Israel’s military intelligence research department Danny Citrinowicz said in a post on X that “the current situation in the Strait of Hormuz is inherently unstable and cannot be sustained indefinitely," and "that even if neither side wants a broader confrontation, the current dynamics are pushing both toward escalation.”“As long as the United States maintains its naval blockade and attempts to push tankers in the southern shipping lane, Tehran will continue to regard these actions as acts of war," the Iran expert said, adding that "Iran is unlikely to accept this reality indefinitely. Instead, it will seek to raise the costs of the blockade through further attacks on tankers and potentially other targets, particularly if US military operations continue around Bandar Abbas," Citrinowicz said.“There is a fundamental asymmetry between Washington and Tehran. The United States may believe it can maintain the blockade for an extended period, but Iran sees it as a direct threat to its economy, sovereignty, and national security. For the Iranian leadership, accepting the blockade without responding would amount to accepting a new strategic reality imposed by Washington. That is simply not how the regime in Tehran operates,” Citrinowicz concluded.

14:42 302 people killed in various incidents in Kyrgyzstan since start of 2026
articles.summary: A total of 3,649 various incidents have been registered in Kyrgyzstan since the beginning of 2026, claiming 302 lives. Minister of Emergency Situations Kanatbek Chynybaev announced this at a meeting of the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on International Affairs, Defense, Security and Migration.
articles.body: A total of 3,649 various incidents have been registered in Kyrgyzstan since the beginning of 2026, claiming 302 lives. Minister of Emergency Situations Kanatbek Chynybaev announced this at a meeting of the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on International Affairs, Defense, Security and Migration. According to him, despite a decline in the overall number of incidents compared with last year, the death toll has increased by 24. As of November 15, 2026, material damage caused by the reported incidents amounted to 1,269 billion soms, according to the Ministry of Emergency Situations. For comparison, 3,816 incidents were recorded during the same period in 2025, claiming 278 lives. Material damage amounted to 1,735 billion soms. Thus, the number of incidents decreased by 167, while material damage fell by 466 million soms. The minister also reported that 42 emergencies had been registered in the country since the beginning of this year, claiming 42 lives. The damage amounted to 468,502 million soms. During the same period last year, 14 emergencies were recorded, leaving 32 people dead, while the damage was estimated at 60 million soms. A total of 2,709 fires have been registered in Kyrgyzstan since the beginning of the year, 509 fewer than during the same period in 2025. Material damage caused by fires amounted to 1,213 billion soms, down 518 million soms from last year’s figure. Twenty-two people died in fires, compared with 46 in 2025. Another 30 people were injured, while five were rescued. According to Kanatbek Chynybaev, emergency response teams have rescued 428 people since the beginning of the year. During the same period in 2025, 368 people received assistance.

articles.summary: Kyiv and Moscow dispute scale of damage which means travel out of the peninsula is now only via a land corridor vulnerable to Ukrainian drone attack Ukraine critically damages Kerch bridge Finland’s highly influential president Alexander Stubb has arrived in Berlin this morning for talks with Germany’s Friedrich Merz.
articles.body: Ukraine has critically damaged the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia in an overnight missile attack, in what Ukrainian officials say is a symbolic blow to the Kremlin. Photos suggest that a 227-metre road arch span has fallen into the Kerch strait, which connects the Sea of Azov with the Black Sea. The adjacent railway arch span has also sustained damage. Ukrainian commentators say the massive steel arch cannot easily be replaced. The closure of the bridge means that traffic from Crimea can travel out of the peninsula only via a land corridor through occupied southern Ukraine, vulnerable to Ukrainian drones. But Russian officials, quoted by Reuters, insisted that damage was only minor, and would be quick to sort out. “ We have already gathered together the resources, designers, and builders ‌for repair work. We are sorting out logistics issues with the regional leadership,” Russian deputy prime minister Marat Khusnullin wrote on Telegram. The bridge has in the past been a key supply route for Russian forces in Ukraine ​and is widely viewed as one of Russian president Vladimir Putin’s signature infrastructure projects. The overnight strike followed ‌ an intensification of ​Russian attacks in the ​past few months on bridges in Ukraine , including in the capital Kyiv. Elsewhere, EU defence ministers are meeting in Brussels this morning for their latest discussions on Ukraine, followed by the Ukraine defence contact group. Meanwhile, Germany’s chancellor Friedrich Merz is hosting Finland’s influential Alexander Stubb, two days before a major meeting of the coalition of the willing in Berlin. They will no doubt offer their reaction to today’s events in Ukraine. I will bring you all the latest. It’s Tuesday, 17 November 2026 , it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live .

articles.title: Buchukuri: ‘The issues being examined by the Constitutional Court are irrelevant’
articles.summary: Ana Buchukuri, one of the leaders of the Gakharia for Georgia party, has questioned the relevance of the issues being examined by the Constitutional Court in proceedings concerning a lawsuit seeking to ban several opposition parties. “It is the 14th day of hearings, and today it should be our turn to be questioned.
articles.body: Ana Buchukuri, one of the leaders of the Gakharia for Georgia party, has questioned the relevance of the issues being examined by the Constitutional Court in proceedings concerning a lawsuit seeking to ban several opposition parties. “It is the 14th day of hearings, and today it should be our turn to be questioned. To be honest, the issues the court is examining are so irrelevant that there is no constitutional basis for them. None of the questions raised by the judges yesterday concerned our party, because we have always held a different position, from vetting to our non-participation in the alliance,” Buchukuri told journalists at the Constitutional Court. She said she was interested in what questions the judges would put to her party, adding that the proceedings did not constitute a genuine legal process. “Ultimately, you know that what is currently taking place at the Constitutional Court is not a legal process. Unfortunately, the parties present here, including the respondent side, cannot influence the decision. Society can see the difference in terms of competence. People can sense it. They may not follow specific legal terms and arguments, but they naturally recognize it,” she said. The Constitutional Court is hearing a lawsuit filed by Georgian Dream seeking to ban three opposition political groups: the United National Movement, the Coalition for Change and Strong Georgia. The ruling party accuses them of violating constitutional principles and seeks to have their activities prohibited. articles.summary: The Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on Constitutional Legislation approved the nomination of Almazbek Moldobaev for the position of judge of the Constitutional Court of Kyrgyzstan. His candidacy was submitted for parliamentary consideration by President Sadyr Japarov.
articles.body: The Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on Constitutional Legislation approved the nomination of Almazbek Moldobaev for the position of judge of the Constitutional Court of Kyrgyzstan. His candidacy was submitted for parliamentary consideration by President Sadyr Japarov. Almazbek Moldobaev currently serves as the Permanent Representative of the President and the Cabinet of Ministers to the Constitutional Court. Born on February 9, 1973, in Frunze, Almazbek Moldobaev graduated from the Faculty of Law at the Zhusup Balasagyn Kyrgyz National University in 1995. He later pursued further education at the Military-Diplomatic Academy and completed postgraduate studies at the Military University of the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation. From 2006 to 2015, he served as a judge at the Pervomaisky District Court in Bishkek. Over the years, he has also held various positions within the Office of the President and the Zhogorku Kenesh. From 2019 to 2023, he headed a department within the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on Law and Order, Combating Crime, and Countering Corruption. He holds the academic degree of Candidate of Legal Sciences, the civil service rank of 1st-class State Civil Service Counselor, and the military rank of Colonel of Justice.

articles.body: The hearing on Georgian Dream’s lawsuit seeking to ban five opposition parties will resume at the Constitutional Court on November 17 at 12:00 p.m. The proceedings will continue in a question-and-answer format, with judges once again directing their questions to representatives of the Strong Georgia – Lelo party. For the record, hearings on the lawsuit began at the Constitutional Court on October 21. The case is being heard by the Plenum of the Constitutional Court, composed of seven judges. The lawsuit submitted to the Constitutional Court is signed by 88 members of parliament. Based on the lawsuit, the court is considering declaring the following five political parties unconstitutional: Unity – National Movement; Coalition for Change – Gvaramia, Melia, Girchi, Droa; Strong Georgia – Lelo, For the People, For Freedom!; the Federalist Party; and For Georgia, led by Giorgi Gakharia . articles.title: Armenian Opposition Slams Pashinian Government Over ‘Political Prisoners’
articles.summary: The hearings in the National Assembly were initiated by the opposition Hayastan (Armenia) alliance and attended by members of the Strong Armenia bloc, as well as political and public figures not represented in parliament.
articles.body: The hearings in the National Assembly were initiated by the opposition Hayastan (Armenia) alliance and attended by members of the Strong Armenia bloc, as well as political and public figures not represented in parliament. Speakers at the event noted that the leaders of both parliamentary blocs – former President Robert Kocharian and Russian-Armenian billionaire Samvel Karapetian – as well as Gagik Tsarukian, the leader of the Prosperous Armenia Party, which fell just short of the threshold to enter parliament in the June elections, are currently imprisoned on what they described as politically motivated charges. Speaking at the session, Lilit Galstian, a lawmaker from the Hayastan faction and head of the parliamentary human rights committee, accused Prime Minister Nikol Pashinian of personally directing the persecution of political opponents from the parliament’s rostrum. As evidence, Galstian cited past warnings by Pashinian that he would send opponents to the notorious “National Security Service dungeon.” Pashinian has repeatedly denied directing any arrests, dismissing such remarks as mere political rhetoric. Civil Contract lawmakers did not attend the proceedings. Volodia Hakobian, secretary of the ruling party’s faction, told RFE/RL’s Armenian Service that his party stayed away from the event because “there are no political prisoners in Armenia.” Hakobian added that it was “ridiculous” for allies of former President Kocharian to raise the issue, hinting at what Civil Contract and its supporters assert were large-scale persecutions of opposition figures during his 1998-2008 presidency. Civil Contract’s decision to skip the session follows a move last week by the ruling majority in the parliament’s committee on state and legal issues to reject a draft opposition statement on democratic backsliding in Armenia under the Pashinian government, which also referred to the presence of political prisoners. During that committee debate, ruling party lawmaker Arman Yeghoyan dismissed the opposition’s assessments, arguing they had “nothing to do with reality.” During Monday’s hearings, Gohar Meloyan, of the Strong Armenia bloc, called for an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the in-custody death of her teammate, Arsen Gevorgian. Meloyan alleged that Gevorgian, a mayoral candidate in Stepanavan who had been arrested on vote-buying charges, died from an apparent heart attack due to a lack of proper medical care. Government officials have disputed that claim. Last week, both Justice Minister Srbuhi Galian and the head of the Penitentiary Service stated that Gevorgian had received all necessary medical treatment prior to his death. Former lawmaker Naira Zohrabian also used her address at the hearings to criticize Justice Minister Galian, who had emotionally stated last week that she and her underage child were being targeted in the wake of Gevorgian’s death. “You are a representative of a political party whose supporters harassed my child during the 2018 political upheaval by telling her that her mother had died and instructing her to go to the morgue to retrieve my body. You are a member of the team that placed coffins outside the doors of living people,” Zohrabian said. Opposition lawmaker Anna Grigorian, who chaired the session, intervened to state that children should not bear responsibility for the actions of their parents, either in 2018 or today. Among those who spoke at Monday’s hearings was the 14-year-old daughter of Aregnaz Manukian, a leading member of the opposition Mayr Hayastan party who is being prosecuted as part of a high treason case against party chairman Andranik Tevanian. After her imprisonment in July, Manukian, whom the opposition also considers a political prisoner, was barred for weeks from seeing or speaking with friends or relatives, including her daughter. Law enforcement authorities reluctantly allowed the girl to visit her mother in prison in August following an uproar from opposition and public figures.

articles.title: Moldova to participate in Ukraine’s demining efforts after war ends
articles.summary: Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Foreign Affairs Mihai Popșoi participated in the fourth edition of Ukraine Mine Action Conference, held in Brussels. The official reaffirmed the Republic of Moldova’s commitment to contributing to humanitarian demining efforts in Ukraine once a ceasefire is established.
articles.body: Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Foreign Affairs Mihai Popșoi participated in the fourth edition of Ukraine Mine Action Conference, held in Brussels. The official reaffirmed the Republic of Moldova’s commitment to contributing to humanitarian demining efforts in Ukraine once a ceasefire is established. UMAC 2026: Clearing the way in partnership - organized by the European Union and Ukraine in partnership with Belgium, and brought together officials, representatives of international organizations, academia and private sector, as well as operators involved in mine action. In his address, Mihai Popșoi emphasized the need to maintain international support for Ukraine and coordinate efforts to reduce the risks posed by landmines and explosive remnants of war. The minister pointed out that these munitions pose a danger to the population even after the war ends, while the effects of Russian aggression extend beyond Ukraine’s borders. The head of Moldova’s diplomacy highlighted the support provided by the Republic of Moldova by facilitating the training of Ukrainian personnel for humanitarian mine action. He also reiterated the country’s readiness to participate in demining efforts in Ukraine once a ceasefire is established. The Republic of Moldova also joined the Joint Declaration adopted during the conference. Through the document, participants pledge to coordinate their efforts to accelerate the recovery and reconstruction of mine-affected areas, strengthen international demining activities and ensure safer conditions for affected communities. At the end of his address, Mihai Popșoi reiterated the Republic of Moldova’s support for Ukraine and for international efforts to achieve lasting peace. articles.title: US addresses rumors of a Nov. 17 blackout
articles.summary: The U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) stated that reports circulating on social media about power and internet outages and disruptions in banking operations are not true, the agency said on X. What is actually happening on Nov. 17?
articles.body: The U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) stated that reports circulating on social media about power and internet outages and disruptions in banking operations are not true, the agency said on X . FEMA and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) will jointly conduct a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System (EAS). The test is scheduled to begin at 2:20 p.m. ET and last approximately one minute. Regular TV and radio broadcasts will be interrupted by a test message in English and Spanish. «It lasts 1 minute, and no action is required. No blackouts, no secret emergencies. Just our legally mandated, routine test on TV and radio at approximately 2:20 PM ET,» the agency said in a post on X. FEMA stressed that the test is unrelated to any emergency and does not involve outages affecting electricity, communications, internet or banking services. A prediction of a digital catastrophe allegedly set to strike on Nov. 17, 2026, has been widely circulating on social media. The authors of the posts claim that hackers will breach banks worldwide, wipe out bank account balances and shut down the internet for three months. Media reports say that on Oct. 31, a user going by the nickname Wesley posted about an impending collapse. He claimed that an acquaintance with ties to the darknet had warned him about it. The author provided no verifiable evidence. Initially, the post mentioned a mysterious «COVID 2.0.» Details about bank breaches, wiped-out account balances and a prolonged internet shutdown emerged as the story spread further. Furthermore, social media users began referencing an episode of «The Simpsons,» «It’s a Blunderful Life» (Season 35, 2023), in which a power outage hits the fictional town of Springfield on Nov. 17. However, the animated series makes no mention of either 2026 or global cyberattacks. Kursiv.media previously reported that several major U.S. banks experienced widespread disruptions to their online services on Nov. 16. In a separate report, Kursiv.media examined rumors of a «digital apocalypse» allegedly scheduled for Nov. 17. Kazakhstanis were warned of mass cyberattacks, wiped-out bank account balances and a three-month internet shutdown. However, the country’s Ministry of Emergency Situations dismissed these reports.

Bosnia’s New Presidency Takes Office for 2026-2030 Term
articles.summary: The three members of Bosnia's state presidency – two of whom are women – took office on Monday following last month's elections, and will mostly be in charge of foreign policy.
articles.body: Darijana F ilipovic, Zeljka Cvijanovic and Denis Becirovic pose for a photo after their inaugural session. Photo: N1. Bosnia and Herzegovina’s newly elected tripartite presidency took office on Monday at a session in Sarajevo, with Denis Becirovic, Zeljka Cvijanovic and Darijana Filipovic beginning their four-year mandates. Speaking after his inauguration, Bosniak representative Becirovic, who is beginning his second consecutive term, said his priorities would include defending Bosnia’s sovereignty, protecting human rights and advancing the country’s European Union and NATO integration. He also pledged to promote equality and fight discrimination. His vision, he said, was of an economically strong, technologically developed and socially just Bosnia and Herzegovina, fully integrated into both organisations. He called for an end to divisive political rhetoric, saying political energy should be directed towards building a safer future. “People draw no benefit from populism and arguments. They want peace, security, social justice and good prospects for their children,” he said. Serb representative Cvijanovic, also beginning her second consecutive term, called on domestic politicians to take full responsibility for the country’s future rather than expect solutions from abroad. She criticised international intervention in Bosnia’s politics, arguing that decisions imposed over the previous four years had deepened political crises. She also said the domination by one constituent people over the other two was unacceptable. Croat representative Darijana Filipovic called for the presidency to show more responsibility towards voters. “From today, the question is no longer who was given trust, but what we can do with that trust,” Filipovic said. She said she would work to ensure that Croats in Bosnia felt politically represented and equal. “We are not asking for Croats to have more, and we do not accept that they have less. I believe the same rule must apply to everyone else in this country, because Bosnia and Herzegovina … must be a country in which people have equal worth,” she said. Filipovic succeeds Zeljko Komsic, who served four terms as the Croat member of the Presidency but who was widely seen as owing his place to Bosniak votes. The new Presidency is the first since the 1995 Dayton Peace Agreement established the institution to include two women, Cvijanovic became the first woman to serve on the body in 2022. The three members were elected in the October 4 general elections, with the Central Election Commission confirming the results on November 3. Under the Presidency’s rules, the chairmanship rotates every eight months. Bosnia’s state presidency is responsible for foreign policy, appointing ambassadors and other representatives to international organisations and proposing the annual state budget to parliament, based on a recommendation from the Council of Ministers.

articles.title: EU Commissioner ‘Regrets’ Serb Song About Kosovo at Brussels Event
articles.summary: Following complaints, Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos expressed regret for the performance of a Serb nationalist ballad about Kosovo at an EU event in Brussels, saying it does not reflect the European bloc's position.
articles.body: European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos speaking in Brussels, 16 November 2026. Photo: EPA/Olivier Hoslet. The European Commissioner for Enlargement, Marta Kos, on Monday said she regretted that a controversial song about Kosovo was performed before the opening of the European Enlargement Forum in Brussels. “I regret the choice of the song by the musicians. It touches sensitive feelings, particularly given the history and different experiences of the communities in Kosovo,” Kos, a Slovenian diplomat, said in Brussels. “I want to stress that this song in no way reflects the position of the European Commission or myself with respect to Kosovo and history,” she added. The song,“Oj Kosovo, Kosovo”, celebrates Serbia’s claims to its former province. Its lyrics say that Kosovo “has always been ours” and vow never to give up the territory. It was performed as an instrumental version, by a Slovenian band, at a concert on Sunday, preceding Monday’s European Enlargement Forum. The choice of song was made by the performers rather than the organisers, according to Kos. Jeton Zulfaj, Kosovo’s chief negotiator with the EU, asked Kos “to explain how this happened and what measures she will take, and why Kosovo, the biggest democratic climber in the Western Balkans this decade and fully aligned with EU foreign policy and EU values, was not invited”. On X, Zulfaj called the incident “scandalous and unacceptable. An EU event on enlargement cannot give a stage to Serbian nationalism.” The Albanian Prime Minister, Edi Rama, also condemned the incident. “I don’t know if it was deliberate or ignorance but a tasteless nationalistic song was performed on the eve of this event in the contrary of everything it represents,” Rama said. Riho Terras, a European Parliament member and Kosovo rapporteur, also demanded an explanation from the European Commission and Kos. “Performing a Serbian nationalist song asserting claims over Kosovo at an EU enlargement event is an extraordinarily tactless and tasteless blunder,” he said. The author Ljubomir Manasijevic recounted in 2019 that the song was created in 1989, inspired by the celebration of the Battle of Kosovo’s 600th anniversary near Pristina, at which Serbian leader Slobodan Milosevic gave a fiery speech which has been identified by some historians as marking the beginning of Yugoslavia’s collapse. “What it is clear is that we cannot change our shared past but we can choose our shared future and the future must be European. European in the sense that we will respect differences, but this would be the future without divisions, where everybody feels at home,” Kos said. “It is very clear to me that we are not asking to forget differences. We are building, and this is my important task, a Europe where actually differences will no longer be a reason to live apart,” she added.

articles.title: Second Trial of Kosovo’s Thaci, for Obstructing Justice, Nears End
articles.summary: Verdict looms on Tuesday in former President Hashim Thaci's second trial at The Hague, in which he is accused of interfering with witnesses in the earlier war-crimes case against him.
articles.body: This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp The second trial of former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci at The Hague is coming to an end, with the verdict to be announced on Tuesday. Thaci, who was also a wartime guerrilla leader, is being tried alongside four co-defendants for obstruction of justice. He is accused of interfering with witnesses in his war-crimes trial. The Kosovo Specialist Prosecutor’s Office in The Hague, in its closing statements on September 10, demanded six years’ prison for Thaci, claiming he told his co-defendants to instruct witnesses what to say while testifying in his war-crimes case. It sought “nine months of imprisonment for [Hajredin] Kuci; three years for [Fadil] Fazliu; three years for [Isni] Kilaj; three years for [Bashkim] Smakaj; and six years for Thaci,” prosecutor Joshua Hafetz said during the closing statements. The prosecution claimed that Thaci tried to exert influence over two former Kosovo Liberation Army fighters, Bislim Zyrapi and Rrustem Mustafa, who were testifying in his war-crimes case. The testimony of both men favoured Thaci’s defence. In his testimony in 2023, former KLA area commander Mustafa claimed that the KLA zone commanders made the key operational decisions, not the General Staff. He said the KLA leaders, who included Thaci, did not have control over lower-ranking fighters – testimony that bolstered the defence’s case. Zyrapi, former chief of the KLA’s General Staff, gave his testimony in 2024. He also said the General Staff often was not informed of the actions of fighters in the operational zones and that, despite attempts, it had not been possible for the KLA to fully exercise control over its lower-level units, partly because of Serbian offensives. On September 16 this year, the Specialist Chambers sentenced Thaci to 25 years in prison for the war crimes of murder, arbitrary detention, torture and cruel treatment as a leader of the KLA during the Kosovo war from April 1998 to June 20, 1999. His co-defendants, Jakup Krasniqi, Kadri Veseli, and Rexhep Selimi, were sentenced to 25, 18 and 13 years respectively. The defence is preparing to appeal the first-instance verdict. The September 16 verdict triggered protests in Kosovo and in Europe by Albanian diaspora members and supporters of the KLA. Kosovo’s parliament on October 6 voted to amend the law on the Specialist Chambers to curb its powers. The law has been returned to parliament for review by the President, however . The EU and the UK have warned Kosovo MPs not to vote for the law change without consultations with the international community, as the court was established via an international agreement. The Specialist Chambers was created specifically to try former members of the KLA; it is located in The Hague and staffed by international judges and prosecutors due to doubts about the Kosovo justice system’s own ability to try former KLA fighters, many of whom are considered heroes in Kosovo. Witness-tampering has been one of its key concerns from the outset.

articles.title: Mongolian president announces resignation amid corruption allegations
articles.summary: Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh, Mongolia’s sixth president, has announced his resignation after the opposition accused him of corruption, Xinhua reported. The nature of the allegations The Democratic Party’s parliamentary faction raised the allegations against Khürelsükh, claiming that he may have received funds linked to a state-run railway construction project.
articles.body: Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh , Mongolia’s sixth president, has announced his resignation after the opposition accused him of corruption, Xinhua reported. The Democratic Party’s parliamentary faction raised the allegations against Khürelsükh, claiming that he may have received funds linked to a state-run railway construction project. Khürelsükh has stated that he is prepared to cooperate with the investigation. He also intends to defend his reputation. Khürelsükh has served as Mongolia’s president since June 2021. Previously, he served as the country’s prime minister but resigned amid protests over the government’s handling of the COVID-19 pandemic. In April, Khürelsükh paid a state visit to Kazakhstan and received the Order of the Golden Eagle (Altyn Qyran), Kazakhstan’s highest state honor, from President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev .

articles.title: New kindergartens to open inside women’s prisons across Uzbekistan
articles.summary: Starting Dec. 1, Uzbekistan will open specialized kindergartens for children of incarcerated women at two correctional facilities. The centers will allow mothers to spend time with their children, who must be under the age of 3, including staying with them overnight.
articles.body: Starting Dec. 1, Uzbekistan will open specialized kindergartens for children of incarcerated women at two correctional facilities. The centers will allow mothers to spend time with their children, who must be under the age of 3, including staying with them overnight. The initiative was established by a presidential resolution signed by Shavkat Mirziyoyev on Nov. 12. The new facilities, called «Mother and Child Centers,» will be established at Correctional Colony No. 21 and Settlement Colony No. 42, according to Kun.uz . At the former, the center will be set up within an existing children’s home. The facilities will offer round-the-clock care groups, each accommodating up to five children. Children will receive food, clothing, footwear, medical care and other essentials to support their health and development. The Ministry of Health will oversee vaccinations and medical examinations, while the National Agency for Social Protection will conduct quarterly inspections to monitor living conditions for mothers and their children. Under the presidential resolution, the centers are intended to help incarcerated women maintain close bonds with their children. Mothers will be allowed to spend time with them during their free hours, including overnight. Kazakhstan also has a specialized facility for incarcerated women with young children. It is located in the village of Zhaugashty in the Almaty region. As previously reported by Kursiv.media, as of September 2025, approximately 600 women were being held at the facility. It also has a «house for infants,» a nursery where more than 50 children were living with their mothers at the time.

articles.title: Becirovic: EU and NATO Integration must be among BiH’s top Priorities
articles.summary: Denis Bećirović, who continues to serve as a member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, stated that in his new term he will continue to champion human rights, freedom, and the dignity of every individual.
articles.body: Denis Bećirović, who continues to serve as a member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, stated that in his new term he will continue to champion human rights, freedom, and the dignity of every individual. He also pledged to advocate for the independence and sovereignty of BiH, integration into the EU and NATO, the strengthening of state institutions, and a better life for all citizens. “It is a profound honor for me to serve another term as a member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina,” said Bećirović. He expressed his gratitude to Željko Komšić and Željka Cvijanović for their cooperation during the previous term of the Presidency. He noted that his priorities remain the protection of BiH’s independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity, and international legal personality; the upholding of constitutionality and the rule of law; the acceleration of EU and NATO integration; the promotion of equality among citizens and constituent peoples; and the fight against discrimination. According to Bećirović, his focus will also include strengthening diplomacy and the Armed Forces of BiH, supporting the economy, implementing rulings of the European Court of Human Rights, and fostering a democratic society rooted in social solidarity. “My vision for Bosnia and Herzegovina is one that is economically robust, technologically advanced, and socially just—fully integrated into the EU and NATO,” he declared. He described a nation that nurtures knowledge, its people, and its existing potential—a place where diverse ethnic, religious, regional, and social identities are freely developed and respected, all while building a shared national identity. A Call to Focus on Vital Issues Discussing how BiH can make progress over the next four years, Bećirović stated that there is a formula for collective advancement. “This formula entails not wasting citizens’ time by advocating for unrealistic, unilateral, and dangerous policies. Instead of promoting irrational policies, let us direct our energy toward building a more secure future,” he said. He urged that attention be shifted toward addressing fundamental existential issues, while rejecting polemics that—as he put it—sow discord and create a negative atmosphere. “People derive no benefit from crude populism or pointless squabbles. They want peace, security, social justice, development, and a promising future for their children,” he emphasized. Bećirović stated that, for progress to occur, it is essential that elected officials perform the duties defined by their job descriptions, and that authority remains concentrated within state institutions rather than within the leadership of political parties. He particularly emphasized the importance of the rule of law and respect for the continuity of decisions. “Adopted laws and other legal acts must be respected; they can only be amended within the state institutions where they were originally enacted,” he said. Bećirović noted that BiH’s strategic foreign policy goals are full membership in the European Union and NATO. Regarding EU membership, he described it as “of exceptional importance for our people and our state.” He pointed out that, during the 2022–2026 term, BiH has made progress on its European path: the European Council granted the country candidate status in December 2022, and in March 2024, it decided to open accession negotiations. He added that BiH’s foreign policy is fully aligned with the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy. “Fulfilling the requirements for European Union membership must be a top priority,” he stated, adding that no single political party possesses the capacity to lead this process on its own. He called for setting aside political and ideological differences to work together on European integration. “The process of European integration must not become an end in itself. We need to accelerate this process for the sake of our citizens and to create a better economic environment within the country,” he said. Speaking about NATO, Bećirović stated that BiH and the Alliance are “inseparably linked.” According to him, membership would contribute to strengthening the economy, stability, and security, as well as attracting foreign investment and fostering better regional cooperation. “I will do everything in my power to ensure that an invitation for NATO membership is extended to Bosnia and Herzegovina as soon as possible during my new term,” he said. He added that BiH’s paths toward NATO and the EU are complementary, and that progress on the NATO track simultaneously brings the country closer to membership in the European Union. Bećirović described regional cooperation as an essential prerequisite for European integration. He stated that it should be founded upon respect for the independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity of states, as well as equality, mutual respect, reciprocity, non-interference in internal affairs, and relations based on international law. He noted that the Presidency of BiH serves as the supreme command of the Armed Forces. Over the past four years, he said, it has been ensured that the Armed Forces provide assistance to citizens throughout the entire territory of BiH. In the new term, he added, it is necessary to continue the reform of the defense system in line with NATO standards and strategic documents. “The Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina must strengthen their capabilities and remain constantly prepared to carry out their tasks and missions,” he said. An effective defense system, he added, should serve to ensure the general safety, personal security, and property security of citizens. Bećirović emphasized the importance of the Presidency continuing to support the Central Bank of BiH and safeguarding its independence. “Only an independent and professional Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina can serve as a reliable guardian of the state’s monetary stability and our convertible mark,” he stated. He noted that, over the last three years, the Central Bank has achieved the best results in its history. According to him, more funds were contributed to the BiH state budget than in the previous 26 years combined; monetary gold reserves were increased to their highest historical level—the maximum permitted by law—and the coverage ratio for the domestic currency was raised to a record 110 percent. He added that the modernization of banknotes, in line with contemporary security standards, has been completed, with their entry into circulation expected in 2028. As further achievements, he noted that the payment system has been modernized after 25 years, and the first domestic instant payment system—aligned with European directives and standards—has been introduced. He stated that BiH is on the verge of joining the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), a move that would generate savings for citizens and the business sector while fostering economic development. Bećirović emphasized the importance of strengthening the bond between BiH and its diaspora, noting that millions of citizens live and work across the globe. “They represent a tremendous force and a true partner in building the future of our state,” he said. He called for efforts to improve the status and rights of the diaspora, preserve their identity, strengthen economic cooperation, and nurture historical, sporting, cultural, scientific, and other ties with BiH. In closing, he urged citizens to work together to contribute to a better life and the restoration of optimism. “Instead of a monologue, let us choose dialogue; and instead of short-term political interest, let us choose statesmanship. Let us stand united for the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina—a country where our children will grow up in a safe environment, free from violence, war, and the deprivation of rights,” concluded Bećirović, BHRT writes.

articles.title: Georgia Skips EU Ministerial on Connectivity, Citing Lower-Level Invitation
articles.summary: Georgian Foreign Ministry said Tbilisi would skip the EU connectivity ministerial in Brussels on November 16, citing the absence of an invitation “at an appropriate level,” while expressing commitment to “constructive cooperation” with the bloc. The meeting, held on the sidelines of the EU Foreign Affairs Council, brings together ministers from the South Caucasus, Central …
articles.body: Georgian Foreign Ministry said Tbilisi would skip the EU connectivity ministerial in Brussels on November 16, citing the absence of an invitation "at an appropriate level," while expressing commitment to "constructive cooperation" with the bloc. The meeting, held on the sidelines of the EU Foreign Affairs Council, brings together ministers from the South Caucasus, Central Asia, Moldova, Turkey and Ukraine, according to the EU's official announcement. Georgia was also absent from a similar meeting in Luxembourg last year, with the ministry at the time also citing a lower-level invitation as the reason for declining to attend. "Georgia has not received an invitation at the appropriate level to participate in the events planned in Brussels on November 16, including the Connectivity Ministerial. Accordingly, no Georgian representative will participate in the meeting," the Foreign Ministry said in the statement. The statement came a day after Georgian media outlet Publika cited Vakhtang Makharoblishvili, Georgian Ambassador to the EU, as confirming his participation in the meeting, following media reports that Georgia again received a lower-level invitation to the meeting. "At the same time, Georgia remains committed to constructive cooperation with the European Union and is ready to participate in meetings if invited at the appropriate level," the Ministry added, noting that "Brussels is aware of this position." Kos: We Invite, But Not on Highest Level Speaking at a news briefing on November 16, EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos told Deutsche Welle that Brussels has repeatedly invited Georgian representatives, but not at the highest level. "Now, for two or three times we have invited the representatives of Georgia to our events on connectivity, and they never came," Kos said. "So we try to engage, we invite them. They don't want to come. We don't invite on the highest level." "We are looking for the engagement; we wanted to have dialogue on the visa liberalization, it was not possible, so, I hope that the Foreign Affairs Council in January [...] will bring some movement," Kos added, referring to EU HR/VP Kaja Kallas' earlier announcement of a "deeper discussion with the foreign ministers regarding Georgia in January." 21/04/2026 - Kos: EU to Involve Georgia in Connectivity to Extent Tbilisi’s Willing to Engage ‘On Other Areas’ Separately, responding to a question from Euroscope, the commissioner said the EU doesn't want Georgia "excluded from these very important activities we do in the fields of trade, transport, energy and digital." Kos, however, said that, in this direction, too, "there are conditions." "We will invite them again and again," she said. "I believe that we have to be engaged. But of course they also have to deliver." Kobakhidze Expects 'Dignified Invitation' Meanwhile, Georgian Dream Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze criticized the level of Georgia's invitation, reiterating his earlier calls for a "dignified invitation." "The Georgian people deserve a fair and healthy approach, which we do not see today," Kobakhidze told journalists during a November 16 press briefing. "Where our country receives a dignified invitation, it will be appropriately represented. Where we see a different attitude, we will respond accordingly." Commenting on Georgia's exclusion from the EU Enlargement Forum, Kobakhidze accused European officials of acting against Europe's interests, saying, "For us, this is further confirmation that the European bureaucracy is not acting in accordance with Europe's objective interests." The relations between Georgia, which became an EU candidate country in 2023, and Brussels worsened amid the Georgian Dream government’s anti-democratic moves and anti-EU discourse. The EU said in November 2025 that Georgia is a candidate country “in name only” and moved to suspend visa-free travel for Georgian holders of diplomatic and service passports. Brussels has also repeatedly stated that the bloc has reduced high-level contacts with Tbilisi amid strained relations. In its November 4 enlargement report, the European Commission pointed to Georgia’s “continued backsliding” and democratic deterioration, saying its EU integration “could resume” if the authorities “change course.” The Commission also warned that Georgia’s failure to address democratic concerns could put its visa-free regime with the EU at risk “more generally.” Meanwhile, Georgian officials have claimed that they seek to engage in "open and constructive dialogue" with the EU "on the basis of mutual respect."
